"### Chart Description: Real Wage Index

This line chart tracks the **Real Wage Index** from February 2020 to February 2024, using October 2016 as the base period ($100$). The chart displays four distinct categories of wages, all showing a general downward trend with a significant sharp decline towards the end of 2023.

#### **Chart Components**
*   **Vertical Axis (Y):** Index values ranging from 30 to 120.
*   **Horizontal Axis (X):** Timeline from Feb-20 to Feb-24 at 4-month intervals.
*   **Legend Categories:**
    *   **All** (Dark blue line)
    *   **Private, formal** (Medium blue line)
    *   **Private, informal** (Grey line)
    *   **Public, formal** (Light blue line)

#### **Estimated Data Points (Index Values)**

| Date | Private, formal | All | Public, formal | Private, informal |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Feb-20** (Start) | ~92 | ~86 | ~82 | ~79 |
| **Oct-21** (Mid-point) | ~88 | ~82 | ~81 | ~70 |
| **Oct-23** (Pre-drop) | ~82 | ~77 | ~78 | ~50 |
| **Feb-24** (End) | ~72 | ~62 | ~62 | ~36 |

#### **Key Observations and Trends**
*   **Highest Wages:** The "Private, formal" sector consistently maintained the highest real wage index throughout the period, though it fell from ~92 to ~72.
*   **Most Significant Decline:** The "Private, informal" sector experienced the most drastic loss in value, dropping from nearly 80 at the start to approximately 36 by February 2024, representing more than a 50% decrease in real wages.
*   **Recent Sharp Contraction:** All sectors show a steep, synchronized drop starting after October 2023. By early 2024, the "Public, formal" and "All" wage categories converged at an index of approximately 62.
*   **Overall Trend:** Real wages across all sectors failed to return to early 2020 levels, indicating a sustained and accelerating loss of purchasing power over the four-year period."
